requirements.requirement: Export only records belonging to the active workspace.

codeReferences.note: exportOrders filters on query.status only; workspaceId is never applied — 'orders.filter(o => !query.status || o.status === query.status)'

requirements.observation: The exportOrders function at src/orders.ts:8 omits the workspaceId predicate present in listOrders (src/orders.ts:4 / baseline/orders.ts:4). The R1 probe (probes/r1-workspace-scope.test.mjs) reproduces the defect: calling exportOrders with workspaceId:'a' against a dataset containing both workspace-a and workspace-b records returns rows from both workspaces. Actual output: 'id,status,total\n"a1","paid","10"\n"b1","paid","99"'. Both probe tests fail (exit code 1).

requirements.requirement: Respect the selected status filter. Export every matching record across all pages, regardless of the current page offset or limit.

codeReferences.note: Status predicate: !query.status || o.status === query.status applied to full orders array — offset/limit are not read
Test 'CSV contains matching rows and header' passes status:'paid' and verifies only the paid row is exported

requirements.observation: exportOrders iterates the full input array and applies the status predicate without calling slice or consulting offset/limit. The existing test suite passes (4/4 green). This is limited to the checks shown; no cross-page boundary test exists, but the implementation structure is consistent with the requirement. Note: R2 evidence is partially undermined by R1 being violated — once workspace scoping is added the status test may need to be re-checked.

requirements.requirement: Empty exports contain the header row.

codeReferences.note: serialize() always prepends 'id,status,total' as first element of the join array
Test 'empty export retains header' asserts exportOrders([],…) === 'id,status,total'

requirements.observation: serialize() uses ['id,status,total', ...rows.map(…)].join('\n'); when rows is empty the spread contributes nothing and the output is the header only. Dedicated test passes. Supported, limited to the checks shown.

requirements.requirement: Quote CSV values and escape embedded quotation marks.

codeReferences.note: Each field: '"' + String(v).replaceAll('"','""') + '"' — wraps in double-quotes and doubles embedded quotes
Test 'CSV escapes quotes and commas': id 'a,"b' becomes '"a,""b"' in output

requirements.observation: All values are unconditionally double-quoted and embedded double-quote characters are replaced with double-double-quote per RFC 4180. The escape test passes. Supported, limited to the checks shown.

findings.title: exportOrders does not filter by workspaceId
evidence: src/orders.ts:8 — predicate is '!query.status || o.status === query.status'; query.workspaceId is never referenced
probes/r1-workspace-scope.test.mjs — two tests both fail; actual output includes rows from a different workspace
findings.detail: By contrast, listOrders (src/orders.ts:4 and baseline/orders.ts:4) correctly includes 'o.workspaceId === query.workspaceId' in its filter. The fix is to add the same predicate to the filter in exportOrders at src/orders.ts:8. The existing test suite does not cover this case: test/orders.test.mjs:6 supplies a dataset where all rows share the same workspaceId:'a', so cross-workspace leakage is never exercised.

unassessed: Header column order is fixed to 'id,status,total'; no requirement specifies column order — not assessed.
Behaviour when query.workspaceId is an empty string or undefined — out of scope per requirements.
Performance with very large order datasets — out of scope per requirements.
Integration with the order-list screen's Query object construction — not represented in this file set.
recommendation: Do not merge. R1 is reproducibly violated: exportOrders leaks orders from all workspaces. The fix is a single-line change to add the workspaceId predicate to the filter in exportOrders (src/orders.ts:8), matching the predicate already present in listOrders. After fixing, add a test that mixes orders from multiple workspaces to prevent regression. R2, R3, and R4 are supported by the existing tests.
